🚂 Railways of Morocco, Algeria & Tunisia · 1862 → 2026

Most lines were laid from 1862 to the 1930s, largely by French companies, under colonial rule in Algeria and the Tunisian and Moroccan protectorates, plus a few in Spanish-zone Morocco. Some 3,000 km of mostly narrow-gauge branches closed from the 1930s on; the Méditerranée-Niger line around Béchar, run by a French state body, shut on 1 January 1963. National railways took over: SNCFT 1956, ONCF 1963, SNTF 1976. Since 2009 new lines have redrawn the map: Al Boraq (2018), Algeria's Hauts Plateaux and Béchar–Gara Djebilet.

📊 Data: dates reconstructed section by section from historical sources; undated sections omitted; approximate routes for vanished lines; some closure years estimated from the last recorded service.
🌍 Land: Natural Earth; Morocco–Western Sahara boundary (disputed) not drawn · track © OpenStreetMap
